manual-start.title: 01 / start the system
manual-start.intro: Load the released v0.3.0 build, then attach the system before adding content. setGrid(6, 4) creates six columns and four rows.

manual-finish.title: 02 / content can be anything
manual-finish.intro: A block can hold anything the browser can render. Choose one of three input forms: trusted HTML, an element object or a factory. Paste one focused example after setGrid() and before </script>.

manual-content-html-code.title: 02.1 / trusted HTML
manual-content-html-code.intro: Use a string only for markup you trust. The string becomes the block's HTML.

manual-content-object-code.title: 02.2 / element object
manual-content-object-code.intro: Use a browser element for text, images, SVG, canvas, forms or media. For untrusted text, set textContent.

manual-content-object.title: 02.2 / result
manual-content-object.caption: 02 / direction
manual-content-object.alt: Black-and-white skatepark with converging concrete ramps, painted lines and a metal rail.

manual-content-factory-code.title: 02.3 / factory
manual-content-factory-code.intro: Use a function when every added block needs a fresh element and its own interaction.

manual-menu.title: 03 / menu actions
manual-menu.intro: The titlebar can show minimize, close, both or neither. The four blocks below are the complete on/off set. A controller can also minimize, restore or remove its own block. Close removes this example; reload the page to restore the full manual.

manual-menu-title.title: 03.5 / title
manual-menu-title.statement: A title is not an id.
manual-menu-title.body: id identifies the block. Add title only when you want visible text in its menu bar; without it, the id stays available to the controls but is not shown.

manual-layout.title: 04 / layout and movement
manual-layout.intro: Set size first, then position. Columns come before rows and coordinates start at 1. Use the practice block below: drag its titlebar, or focus drag here and use the arrow keys. Watch the cell readout change.

manual-layout-wide.title: 04.1 / drag here
manual-layout-wide.body: Grab the dotted titlebar, or focus it and press an arrow key.

manual-layout-small.title: 04.2 / flow
manual-layout-small.body: Releases the fixed position, not the size.

manual-compact.title: 05 / compact after changes
manual-compact.intro: Use compact() after removing or moving fixed blocks when you want the placed grid to close vertical gaps. It moves fixed blocks upward inside their columns; it does not resize the grid.

manual-appearance.title: 06 / choose an appearance
manual-appearance.intro: Choose one fixed monochrome variant. Regular uses dark ink on paper; inverse exchanges figure and ground. Color and chance come later.

manual-colors.title: 07 / set a color
manual-colors.intro: Set one block color directly. Any valid CSS color can define its border, titlebar and hover frame; the content surface stays neutral.

manual-random.title: 08 / set the chance
manual-random.intro: Chance affects only future blocks added with the random variant. The three left cells change the color share; the three right cells change the inverse share of the monochrome remainder. Values run from 0 to 1.

manual-random-combined.title: 08.1 / color + inverse
manual-random-combined.intro: Combine both chances only after reading them separately. In this fixed four-call demonstration, two cells use color, one is regular and one is inverse. Real calls remain random.

reference-system-errors.title: failures + boundaries
reference-system-errors.details: Expect errors for invalid or duplicate ids, missing fields, impossible grid positions, overlaps, unknown definitions, incomplete adapters and colorVariation without colors. Catch only errors your interface can recover from.

reference-block-options.intro: id identifies a block. title is only optional visible text in its menu bar.

reference-block-properties.intro: add() returns one controller for one block.

reference-definition-create.title: definitions + adapters
reference-definition-create.intro: Definitions describe reusable content. Register definitions and their lifecycle adapters on the shared system.

reference-adapter-methods.title: adapter lifecycle methods
reference-adapter-methods.intro: Adapters own mount and cleanup lifecycle; the system methods below use those lifecycle hooks for registered definitions.

reference-field-signals.title: field events + DOM hooks
reference-field-signals.intro: The field dispatches blocks:reorder after pointer or keyboard reordering and blocks:change after explicit state changes.
reference-field-signals.details: For blocks:reorder, input is pointer or keyboard, mode is grid or flow, and positions are { column, row } or null. For blocks:change, type is compact, minimize, restore or remove; id is one block or null, and ids lists affected blocks.
